main_text.l: abfit. quid in istâ re militari? in quâ ego quidem sum, quod dicitur, delphin in terrâ. Caussas tamen ambigendi me habuisse censeo: & alij {*}πολέμων ἀχ ἀγεύσοι[?] iudicanto.

„ Simplici tegmine capitis.] Significat ex ære aut ferro nihil fuisse, dumtaxat è pelle aut lanâ aliquid, & Galerum aut Galeam. Nam sic discernit hanc à Casside Isidorus: quòd Cassis de laminâ est, Galea de corio. Ille hoc verè, & pro eo Tacitus: Vix vni alteriue cassis aut galea, de Germanis sic scribens, & manifestò abiungens. Ipsa vox quoque praefert. quia Galea est proprie ἀπὸ τῆς γα-λέης, à fele aut mustella: etsi Varro maluit petere à Galero.Sanè prisci tegmina ferè petebant à feris. vnde in Homero aliisque, ἰκκδέῃ, κυνέη, ζαυρέῃ, αἰγέῃ[?]: mustellina, canina, taurina caprilla. Lego & in Suidâ: Ἀλωπεχία[?], ἡ περι-κεφαλαία: Vulpina, ipsa galea. Sic igitur dictæ, quia à talibus animalibus captæ. Mos qui passim tangitur à poëtis. vt Statio:

l.i: Telarudes trunci, galea vacua ora leonum.

main_text.l: Ipsas leoninas exuuias sumebant, & sic aptabant vt caput capite velarent, ceteris humeros & dorsum. Homerus de Agamemnone:

l.i: Ἀμφὶ δ᾽ ἔπειτα δαφοινὸν ἕεσσατο δέρμα λέοντ[?] Αἴθων[?], μεγάλοιο, ποδηνεκές. ——
Atque humeros circumiecit pellem inde leonis Ardentis, magni, crurum tenus. ——
Ipse pedes tegmen torquens immane leonis Terribili impexum setâ, cum dentibus albis Indutus capiti, sic regia tecta subibat.

main_text.l: Nec de nihilo hoc poëta Romanus. quoniam & Ro-mani

page.notes: Doubtful readings marked [?]: the Greek in the first paragraph (πολέμων ἀχ ἀγεύσοι), the Greek in the Suidas and Tacitus-related lines, the Homer line endings (λέοντ, Αἴθων) and the Iliad reference (κ., vers. 13). The Greek of the Suidas passage ("ἡ περι-κεφαλαία") and the Statius and Virgil verse lines were read from a small scan and should be checked against the original. "setâ" in the Virgil line may read "fetâ". The asterisk in the first paragraph is written as {*} to mark its place. The catchword is absent: the last line "mani" is the end of the word "Romani", split at the line end, and is part of the text.
